claimVerdicts.note: Abstract: "100 male 11-aside soccer players with ACLR undergoing a criteria-based rehabilitation process, concluding with a 5-stage OFR program."
Numbers match the abstract (84% RTC, 100% vs 80%, ten reinjuries); the source labels itself a Level 4 case series, so 'uncontrolled' is fair.
Matches the abstract (TD 106%, HID 104%, ACC 110%, DEC 48%); peak speed (88%) is omitted but this does not change the point.
Source says the approach "might reduce" recurrence and "The effectiveness of this novel rehabilitation algorithm remains to be evaluated"; the claim keeps this hedge.
p6: "transient episodes of knee pain (as a consequence of the meniscus surgery) delayed the return to running"; the player was a Ligue 1 professional.
p12 describes "very large between-player differences" and the need to monitor "at the individual level"; sample of 10 elite players is correct.
p15 limitation, verbatim; the source adds that roughly 60 data points (6-8 weeks) are needed, which the action paraphrases correctly.
Fifty male Division I players; discussion states "prolonged exposure to higher intensities elicited higher baseline HRs 24h post-exercise"; association wording is appropriate.

statementIssues.note: Says the Buchheit and Lacome records are legacy and not full-text reviewed, while the sources list marks all five fullTextReviewed true; the text contradicts itself.
Lacome et al. describe 10 'elite soccer players' at an elite club and do not explicitly state sex; 'elite male' is a likely but unstated inference.
Adds 'swelling', which no source mentions, but the action explicitly labels the symptom gate as professional caution, so this is acceptable.

tierNote: Limited fits. One uncontrolled case series, one single-player case report and an untested expert algorithm, all in male soccer, cannot rank progression criteria. No Recommended Direction is given, and the actions are framed as options.
usefulnessNote: Honest and quick to read. It says plainly that the library cannot rank criteria and offers sensible framing (criteria rather than time, deceleration lagging at 48% of team training, symptom response, no clearance from load targets). A PT will still lack the strength, hop and ROM criteria the question really asks about, and the coverage gap names them correctly.
suggestedDrafterFixes: Generate the sourceReview dimension from the sources' fullTextReviewed flags so the narrative cannot contradict the source list.
Do not add population descriptors (such as sex) that the source does not state; write 'sex not reported' instead.
When the library cannot answer the core question, list the specific criteria families that are missing and point to the closest leads.
